Each stone has only a 1-row light highlight at its upper edge (rows 16, 20-21 and 25 in the column scans). Each highlight sits directly on a darker face with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The width profile just steps outward (8, 10, 12, 14), which makes a stepped mound silhouette and not a horizontal top surface. The pole and red flag in rows 3-14 are decor. The stones read as front-facing rounded shapes with at most a 1-row rim of top, so the body counts as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny stack of three stones with a thin pole and a red flag, roughly 9x15 source pixels, so it is smaller than one tile. Each stone has only about 3 lightness steps (a light top, a mid body, a dark underside) and a dark outline. The measured 28% neutral dark edge pixels, with the rest tinted, makes the outline mixed rather than clearly material-toned. Several stones read as separate dark-outlined blobs, which leans toward the sticker look. The measured 10 visible tones and 0% near-flat coverage are better than tree-1a786c (7 tones) but far below tree-d43edd (29 tones). The references show clumped multi-tone foliage and a grained trunk, while the cairn has little per-stone grain, no speckle, and no cracks or moss. This is a sparse object, so density is judged by eye. Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter, with shallow shading, so it does not match the Beodeul bar.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small cairn of three or four stacked stones with a thin pole and a red flag. The references are large, richly clumped tree canopies, so the comparison is imperfect. By the numbers it holds up: 10 visible tones per tile against 7 for tree-1a786c, and 0% near-flat coverage. But by eye each stone has only about 3-4 value steps (highlight, mid, shadow, dark edge), with little per-stone grain or speckle. Beodeul stones and foliage are shaded piece by piece with 5-6 steps. 28% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is partly a dark grey line around each stone rather than a consistent dark tone of the neighbouring material. The result looks a bit sticker-like and thinner than the references. Because it is a sparse prop and the evidence is borderline, I fail it on the 'when in doubt' rule. It needs more steps per stone, per-stone texture dots, and tinted outlines.
